# process_barcodes.R

## process_barcodes()

We have moved the code for reading in the `barcode_amplicon_data`, `cell_barcodes` and `readnames` datasets outside of the `process_barcodes()` function. It is displayed below to show how the inputs for the example `process_barcodes()` parameters were generated.

```{r}
# -- Data Structuring --

# Import barcode amplicon data table and assign column names
barcode_amplicon_data <- read.table("data/barcode_amplicon_info.txt",sep=" ")
colnames(barcode_amplicon_data) <- c(
  "readname","amplicon_name","start","quality","cigar","sequence")

# Read cell barcodes from raw FASTQ file
cell_barcodes <- data.table::fread("data/MB_barcoded_barcodes_fastq.txt",header=FALSE)$V1
# Read readnames from raw FASTQ file
readnames <- data.table::fread("data/MB_barcoded_R2_001_readnames_fastq.txt",header=FALSE)$V1
```

Next we want to create subsetted versions of the `barcode_amplicon_data` table, as well as the `cell_barcodes` and `readnames` vectors, to be used as example data stored within the package.

```{r}
# Read in downstream output file
joint_HDR_output <- read_csv("data/joint_HDR_output.csv")
```

```{r}
# Select nine barcodes from joint_HDR_output with a range of HDR outcomes
barcodes_to_keep <- c("GTGCTAAGCAATGCAGCG-1", "CCGTAGTTGGGACTATTC-1",
                      "TTAACGGAGGCGCTCTAT-1", "CGAGTAGCATAGATCTGT-1",
                      "AACTGCGACTGCTCAGCG-1", "AACGCCTACGCCGTTGTT-1",
                      "TCCGATAACATTAAGACC-1", "GGACACTGGCACTAGACT-1",
                      "ACTTGATCTTATCTAGGT-1")

# Extract indices of the cell_barcodes that are to_keep
subset_indices <- which(cell_barcodes %in% barcodes_to_keep)

# Subset cell_barcodes and readnames according to the above indices
cell_barcodes_subset <- cell_barcodes[subset_indices]
readnames_subset <- readnames[subset_indices]

# Export as 'FASTQ' .txt files
writeLines(cell_barcodes_subset, "subset_MB_barcoded_barcodes_fastq.txt")
writeLines(readnames_subset, "subset_MB_barcoded_R2_001_readnames_fastq.txt")
```

```{r}
# Assign readnames as the names of the cell_barcodes vector
names(cell_barcodes) <- readnames
# Map cell barcodes to the amplicon data, using readname as the key
barcode_amplicon_data$cell_barcode <-
  cell_barcodes[barcode_amplicon_data$readname]

# Subset barcode_amplicon_data, keeping only rows with barcodes to_keep
barcode_amplicon_data_subset <- barcode_amplicon_data %>% 
  dplyr::filter(cell_barcode %in% barcodes_to_keep)
```
